newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends off on cat cracker restart.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends off on cat cracker restart.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline fell Friday following the restart of a huge catalytic cracker amid a flood of gasoline imports heading to the New York Habor.

"Gasoline had firmed when Tosco was having problems, so now that it (the cracker) has restarted, the feeling is we certainly won't need these cargoes coming over," said Nauman Barakat, a trader with Prudential Securities in New York.

February gasoline ended 0.67 cent a gallon lower at 67.75 cents. March crude ended off 13 cents a barrel at $24.05 while February heating oil bucked declines and settled up 0.42 cent a gallon at 66.77 cents.
"I think there was a lot of short covering ahead of the weekend," said a New York heating oil dealer, noting traders were selling gasoline to buy heating oil to cover positions.
Heat has dropped more than 2.50 cents a gallon since last Friday, presenting a short-covering opportunity, traders said.
Gasoline supplies in the New York Harbor were expected to grow as an open arbitrage from Europe in early January sent one million tonnes of gasoline across the Atlantic, traders said.

Meanwhile, Tosco Corp restarted its 140,000 barrel per day (bpd) catalytic cracker at its Bayway refinery in Linden, N.J. Wednesday, said state regulators. The restart is so far going smoothly, they said.

Dubbed the "gasoline machine" by traders, the unit is the largest cat cracker in the world. It was shut down in early January to undergo maintenance following a fire-related outage in December. The Bayway refinery has a total capacity of 290,000 bpd.
Crude's price, however, drifted on lackluster trade amid little news.
"There was nothing going on. Crude was in a small range the whole day," said a New York crude trader.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
